correctness.rationale: The flat unitary multiplier rho gives descent of (z,[u:v])->(mz,[u^m:v^m]) for every m>=2. Each lift delta in E[m] admits m fiber scalings; selecting m-th roots of rho(lambda_i) yields independent order-m lifts and vertical mu_m, hence (Z/m)^3. Degrees multiply m^2*m=m^3, pullback numerical eigenvalues m,m^2 give int-amplification. For torsion rho of order N and m=1 mod N the fiber power m^2 descends; independent m-order lifts and vertical mu_(m^2) give (Z/m)^2×Z/m^2 of order m^4; exact O(1) and symmetric-base-ample pullbacks give m^2-polarization. Conversely, an arbitrary q-polarized map of a nontorsion split bundle forces deg g=q on E, monomial complementary fiber forms and g^*L=L^(±q), contradicting isogeny degree q^2. This converse independently reconstructs but does not originate the 2005 published criterion.

originality.rationale: The if-and-only-if polarizability criterion is NOT novel: Shou-Wu Zhang (2005), Proposition 2.3.1(4)(a) and its pp.25-26 proof establish precisely this for degree-zero split elliptic ruled surfaces, including the same g^*M=M^(±q) obstruction. This decisive stronger prior implication overturns the package self-review’s claim of novelty for that component. The audited theorem as a conjunction nevertheless adds uniform existence of explicitly GALOIS int-amplified monomial maps and the two exact deck-group isomorphism types, neither stated nor implied by Zhang’s surface classification or Nakayama (2002), Proposition 5. Thus originality PASS is restricted to the quantitative Galois/deck-group component and the constructive contrast, not to the old torsion criterion; a citation correction is mandatory before any publication.
